text: The Alfred Ackermann–Teubner Memorial Award for the Promotion of Mathematical Sciences was established in 1912 by engineer Alfred Ackermann-Teubner and served as an endowment of the University of Leipzig. The award recognized contributions in mathematical analysis and was given 14 times between 1914 and 1941. Subsequent awards were to be made every other year until a surplus of 60,000 marks was accumulated in the endowment, after which the prize was to be awarded annually. The award's subjects included mathematical analysis. The fifteen individuals honored between 1914 and 1941 received the award during this period. In 1937, Constantin Carathéodory and Erhard Schmidt were invited to serve on the jury for the award. Carathéodory was also invited again in 1944 by the German Union of Mathematicians, alongside Wilhelm Blaschke.
